title: Apple Reinvents the Phone with iPhone
claim_or_use: 2007 iPhone introduction; combination of phone, iPod, internet communicator; Multi-Touch and software-defined interface
notes: Use for dated product capabilities, not for claims about later social effects.

title: The future is here: iPhone X
claim_or_use: All-screen design, removal of Home button, Face ID, TrueDepth camera, and Apple's stated all-display design direction
notes: Company language is useful for product intent; do not treat marketing claims as independent evidence of cultural impact.

title: Apple Launches iPhone 4S, iOS 5 & iCloud
claim_or_use: Siri, improved camera, iCloud, Notification Center and the expansion of the phone as mediator and personal archive
notes: Supports dated capability claims only.

title: Apple Announces Apple Pay
claim_or_use: Payment joined communication, navigation, media and identity on the same carried device
notes: Use for launch mechanics and timing; subsequent adoption is a separate empirical question.

title: iPhone 3G on Sale Tomorrow
claim_or_use: App Store launch with more than 500 native applications; wireless discovery, purchase and installation
notes: Supports the platform-distribution history.

title: Apple Announces Over 100,000 Apps Now Available on the App Store
claim_or_use: Scale of App Store, Push Notifications, and In App Purchase by late 2009
notes: Apple reported more than two billion push notifications sent by this date; company figure.

author_or_institution: Cary Stothart; Ainsley Mitchum; Courtney Yehnert
title: The attentional cost of receiving a cell phone notification
claim_or_use: Notifications can disrupt performance on an attention-demanding task even without phone interaction
notes: Narrow experimental evidence; not a universal estimate of real-world harm.

title: iOS 12 introduces new features to reduce interruptions and manage Screen Time
claim_or_use: Apple's later notification controls, activity reports, pickups and Screen Time management
notes: Shows product response to user-management needs, not proof of prior deliberate addiction engineering.

author_or_institution: Antti Oulasvirta; Tye Rattenbury; Lingyi Ma; Eeva Raita
title: Habits make smartphone use more pervasive
claim_or_use: Brief repetitive checking habits and informational rewards; checking can spur additional device use
notes: Authors distinguish habitual annoyance from addiction; useful counterweight to stronger rhetoric.

title: Apple’s App Store Downloads Top Two Billion
claim_or_use: Rapid expansion of mobile software supply and categories during the early App Store period
notes: Company download and app-count figures; use as scale markers.

author_or_institution: Antti Oulasvirta; Tye Rattenbury; Lingyi Ma; Eeva Raita
title: Habits make smartphone use more pervasive
claim_or_use: Checking habits as learned repetitive behavior rather than proof of clinical addiction
notes: Directly relevant to the chapter's reflex argument.

author_or_institution: Adrian F. Ward; Kristen Duke; Ayelet Gneezy; Maarten W. Bos
title: Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
claim_or_use: Original evidence for some cognitive-capacity effects of smartphone presence
notes: Do not generalize beyond the tested tasks or ignore later mixed evidence.

title: Does the Mere Presence of a Smartphone Impact Cognitive Performance? A Meta-Analysis of the ‘Brain Drain Effect’
claim_or_use: Tests robustness and magnitude of smartphone mere-presence effects across studies
notes: Included specifically to prevent treating Ward et al. as a universal law.

title: The Effect of Mere Presence of Smartphone on Cognitive Functions: A Four-Level Meta-Analysis
claim_or_use: Synthesizes mixed findings across 33 studies and 53 samples on smartphone presence and cognition
notes: Use for replication/heterogeneity context.

title: Point-and-Shoot Memories: The Influence of Taking Photos on Memory for a Museum Tour
claim_or_use: Photo-taking impairment for whole-object photography and the important focused/zoom condition
notes: Supports a conditional claim, not 'photography erases memory.'

author_or_institution: Betsy Sparrow; Jenny Liu; Daniel M. Wegner
title: Google Effects on Memory: Cognitive Consequences of Having Information at Our Fingertips
claim_or_use: Expected future access can shift recall toward where information is stored rather than the information itself
notes: Broader external-memory context; internet/computer study, not smartphone-specific.

title: Habitual use of GPS negatively impacts spatial memory during self-guided navigation
claim_or_use: Associations between greater GPS experience and poorer spatial-memory measures; small longitudinal follow-up
notes: Do not claim GPS damages the hippocampus; sample and causal limits remain important.

author_or_institution: Lauren E. Sherman; Ashley A. Payton; Leanna M. Hernandez; Patricia M. Greenfield; Mirella Dapretto
title: The Power of the Like in Adolescence: Effects of Peer Influence on Neural and Behavioral Responses to Social Media
claim_or_use: Quantified peer endorsement influenced adolescents' liking behavior and neural response in a simulated Instagram task
notes: Neural activation is not evidence of addiction; describe task and observed behavior precisely.

author_or_institution: Erin A. Vogel; Jason P. Rose; Lindsay R. Roberts; Katheryn Eckles
title: Social Comparison, Social Media, and Self-Esteem
claim_or_use: Social-media exposure and upward comparison as a mechanism relevant to self-evaluation
notes: Facebook-era evidence; platform and population context matter.

author_or_institution: Larissa K. Barber; Alecia M. Santuzzi
title: Please respond ASAP: Workplace telepressure and employee recovery
claim_or_use: Defines workplace telepressure and links response pressure with recovery, burnout, absenteeism and sleep measures
notes: Asynchronous-message context extends beyond smartphones; used for expectation rather than hardware causality.

author_or_institution: Larissa K. Barber; Amanda L. Conlin; Alecia M. Santuzzi
title: Workplace telepressure and work–life balance outcomes: The role of work recovery experiences
claim_or_use: Telepressure, detachment, recovery and work-life balance
notes: Supports the organizational-norm mechanism.

author_or_institution: Journal of Occupational Health study authors
title: Effects of task interruptions caused by notifications from communication applications on strain and performance
claim_or_use: One-day disabling of communication notifications; effects on performance and strain moderated by FoMO/telepressure
notes: Field experiment; not evidence that all notification removal benefits all employees.

author_or_institution: Ryan J. Dwyer; Kostadin Kushlev; Elizabeth W. Dunn
title: Smartphone use undermines enjoyment of face-to-face social interactions
source_type: Randomized field experiment and experience sampling
claim_or_use: Phone availability/use during meals increased distraction and reduced reported enjoyment in the field experiment
notes: Supports shared-attention mechanism; not a ban on all co-present phone use.

author_or_institution: James A. Roberts; Meredith E. David
title: My life has become a major distraction from my cell phone: Partner phubbing and relationship satisfaction among romantic partners
claim_or_use: Partner phubbing, phone conflict and relationship-satisfaction associations
notes: Self-report association; causality remains limited.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Mobile Phone Use and Presence
claim_or_use: Distinguishes weaker mere-presence evidence from more consistent negative perceptions associated with active phubbing
notes: Useful counterevidence against treating simple device presence as universally harmful.

author_or_institution: Brandon T. McDaniel; Jenny S. Radesky
title: Technoference: Parent Distraction With Technology and Associations With Child Behavior Problems
claim_or_use: Associations among parent problematic technology use, technology-based interruptions and child behavior
notes: Cross-sectional/family-process evidence; preserve bidirectionality questions.

title: The association between adolescent well-being and digital technology use
claim_or_use: Small associations between digital-technology use and adolescent well-being across large datasets
notes: Central counterweight to population-level catastrophe claims.

author_or_institution: Candice L. Odgers; Michaeline R. Jensen
title: Adolescent mental health in the digital age: facts, fears, and future directions
claim_or_use: Synthesis emphasizing mixed, often small and correlational findings and methodological limits
notes: Use to preserve uncertainty and avoid monocausal claims.

title: Social Media and Youth Mental Health
claim_or_use: Current-evidence framing, possible benefits and harms, and uncertainty around safety for children and adolescents
notes: Advisory is not a causal meta-analysis; report its judgment accurately.

author_or_institution: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
title: Social Media and Adolescent Health
claim_or_use: Consensus review of evidence, heterogeneity, mechanisms and research gaps
notes: Use as a high-level synthesis rather than proof of a single effect size.

title: Health advisory on social media use in adolescence
claim_or_use: Developmentally informed recommendations and evidence cautions around adolescent social-media use
notes: Professional advisory; distinguish recommendations from causal findings.

author_or_institution: Sei Yon Sohn; Philippa Rees; Bethany Wildridge; Nicola J. Kalk; Ben Carter
title: Prevalence of problematic smartphone usage and associated mental health outcomes amongst children and young people
claim_or_use: Problematic smartphone use prevalence and associations with depression, anxiety, stress and sleep among youth
notes: Most included studies were cross-sectional; association does not establish direction.

title: The Power of the Like in Adolescence
claim_or_use: Quantified endorsement as a visible social signal that influences behavior
notes: Used for metrics/peer influence, not to label likes addictive.

title: Social Comparison, Social Media, and Self-Esteem
claim_or_use: Upward social comparison as one route by which quantified/curated environments can affect self-evaluation
notes: Does not establish all social-media use lowers self-esteem.

author_or_institution: John D. Eastwood; Alexandra Frischen; Mark J. Fenske; Daniel Smilek
title: The Unengaged Mind: Defining Boredom in Terms of Attention
claim_or_use: Defines boredom as an aversive inability to engage in satisfying activity and synthesizes attention-based accounts
notes: Used to avoid romanticizing boredom.

title: Does Being Bored Make Us More Creative?
claim_or_use: Some boring tasks increased performance on later creative tasks under tested conditions
notes: Narrow experimental finding; not evidence that boredom is universally beneficial.

author_or_institution: Liese Exelmans; Jan Van den Bulck
title: Bedtime mobile phone use and sleep in adults
claim_or_use: Bedtime phone use after lights out associated with poorer self-reported sleep outcomes in adults
notes: Cross-sectional and self-reported; reverse causation is plausible.

author_or_institution: Ben Carter; Philippa Rees; Lauren Hale; Darsharna Bhattacharjee; Mandar S. Paradkar
title: Association Between Portable Screen-Based Media Device Access or Use and Sleep Outcomes
claim_or_use: Bedtime device access/use associated with poorer sleep outcomes among school-age children and adolescents
notes: Included studies were observational; authors rated evidence limitations.

title: Industry Leaders Announce Open Platform for Mobile Devices
claim_or_use: Android and Open Handset Alliance show that smartphone platform convergence was broader than Apple
notes: Use to establish parallel industry development, not equivalence of all design choices.

title: T-Mobile Launches the Highly Anticipated T-Mobile G1
claim_or_use: First Android-powered commercial handset; Android Market, Google services and touch/QWERTY combination
notes: Supports chapter's multi-company ecosystem argument.

title: Android: The Open Source Cell Phone
claim_or_use: Open-source release of Android and multi-company Open Handset Alliance strategy
notes: Shows platform diffusion beyond a single manufacturer.

title: Is smartphone addiction really an addiction?
claim_or_use: Skeptical review of whether smartphone addiction is a distinct addiction; recommends attention to functions and maladaptive use
notes: Core source for the chapter's clinical-language restraint.

title: Prevalence of problematic smartphone usage and associated mental health outcomes amongst children and young people
claim_or_use: Evidence that problematic use can be associated with real impairment-related outcomes while diagnostic boundaries remain unsettled
notes: Most evidence observational; use 'problematic smartphone use' rather than declaring a disorder.

title: Accessibility
claim_or_use: Examples of mainstream smartphone accessibility capabilities including vision, hearing, mobility and cognitive supports
notes: Current product documentation; features change over time. Used to demonstrate capability, not comparative effectiveness.

title: Apple Announces Apple Pay
claim_or_use: Mobile payment as an example of useful functional convergence
notes: Product capability source only.

author_or_institution: David A. Ellis; Brittany I. Davidson; Heather Shaw; Kristoffer Geyer
title: Do smartphone usage scales predict behavior?
claim_or_use: Compares self-report smartphone-use/addiction scales with objective Apple Screen Time behavior and finds important mismatches
notes: Supports skepticism about self-reported total-use measures.

title: iOS 12 introduces new features to reduce interruptions and manage Screen Time
claim_or_use: Screen Time reports app categories, notifications and pickups rather than only total minutes
notes: Product metric definitions can change across OS versions.

title: Digital Detox and Well-Being
claim_or_use: Review of reduction/abstinence interventions and heterogeneous well-being outcomes
notes: Supports targeted reduction rather than universal abstinence claims.

title: Blocking mobile internet on smartphones improves sustained attention, mental health, and subjective well-being
claim_or_use: Two-week mobile-internet block while retaining calls/texts; causal evidence on sustained attention and well-being for compliers
notes: Intervention targets mobile internet, not the entire phone; compliance and sample context matter.

title: Smartphone screen time reduction improves mental health: a randomized controlled trial
claim_or_use: Three-week reduction to two hours/day among healthy students; post-intervention changes in stress, well-being, depressive symptoms and sleep
notes: Screen time rose rapidly again after intervention; student sample limits generalization.

title: Digital Strategies for Screen Time Reduction: A Randomized Field Experiment
claim_or_use: Grayscale reduced objectively measured screen time; time-limit goal setting reduced it more gradually; no immediate broad well-being/academic benefit
notes: Useful example of behavior change without assuming lower use automatically improves all outcomes.

author_or_institution: Journal of Occupational Health study authors
title: Effects of task interruptions caused by notifications from communication applications on strain and performance
claim_or_use: Disabling communication notifications for one day and the moderating roles of FoMO and telepressure
notes: Supports selective notification-management discussion.

author_or_institution: Ryan J. Dwyer; Kostadin Kushlev; Elizabeth W. Dunn
title: Smartphone use undermines enjoyment of face-to-face social interactions
claim_or_use: Collective phone-away condition during meals as evidence that room-level arrangements can alter distraction/enjoyment
notes: One context; not proof that all phone-free rooms improve all outcomes.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Mobile Phone Use and Presence
claim_or_use: Active phone use during interaction shows more consistent interpersonal effects than mere presence
notes: Supports proportionate rules focused on behavior/context rather than superstition about the object.

title: Blocking mobile internet on smartphones improves sustained attention, mental health, and subjective well-being
claim_or_use: Illustrates that removing one connectivity layer can change outcomes while retaining core communication functions
notes: Used as evidence that mediation can be decomposed rather than requiring total device rejection.

title: iOS 12 introduces new features to reduce interruptions and manage Screen Time
claim_or_use: Historical example of the platform adding explicit attention-management controls after convergence
notes: The future-facing AI/ambient sections are reasoned extrapolation and are not presented as empirical forecasts.
